analysis.title: Global Markets Daily: Macro Assets in Fed Hiking Cycles
key_insights: The Fed began a new hiking cycle in September 2026, the first hike since March 2022. The market prices roughly three additional hikes (~100bps of total tightening). GS economists expect one additional hike.
GS reviews asset performance after the first Fed hike across nine tightening cycles since 1983, excluding the current one. On average the Fed tightened ~260bps over ~13 months.

Equities tend to struggle after the first hike but recover quickly. In the median of both modest and larger cycles they trough within 2 months and recover within 4 months. 6m returns were flat to positive in all cycles except 1994 and 2022, and 12m returns were positive in all except 2022.
Front- and long-end yields tend to rise into the first hike. After the hike, yields peak locally in modest cycles but keep rising for some time in larger cycles.

The yield curve tends to flatten into the first hike and keep flattening afterwards, more and for longer in larger cycles. GS rates strategists note front-end forward yields usually peak around the end of hikes and after the inflation peak is confirmed, after which flattening stops as the curve rallies in parallel.
The real trade-weighted USD tends to strengthen into the first hike, with mixed performance afterwards across cycles.
GS groups 1997, 1999 and 2015 as 'modest' cycles and 1983, 1988, 1994, 2004, 2016 and 2022 as 'other' cycles. The sample is small and the macro shocks differ each time, so analogues have limits.

In the interrupted 1997 and 2015 cycles (one hike each), Treasury yields peaked around the hike and then fell. Equities fell initially in both. 1997 troughed quickly and rallied strongly. 2015 troughed within two months but recovered more slowly and stayed rangebound.

1997 combined benign inflation with solid growth, giving dovish policy shocks and positive growth shocks, which was very positive for risk assets. 2015 combined growth worries with a dovish policy shift, and equities struggled for longer.

In 1999 the Fed hiked into an investment boom with strong growth and high equity valuations. Yields kept rising, the S&P 500 stayed rangebound, and the tech bubble eventually burst, contributing to the 2001 recession.

Versus the three modest cycles, 2026 has a strong labor market and a funds rate well above zero (closer to 1997 and 1999), growth more like 2015, equity valuations like 1999 (Shiller P/E 41), and core inflation (3.0%) higher than at the start of all three.
GS baseline is a modest number of hikes, growth around potential and gradual inflation relief, which implies a modestly positive path for equities. This sits between the three historical examples.
Risk scenario 1: a shorter cycle on more pronounced inflation relief (which likely requires oil price relief) is the most positive for risk assets, a mild version of 1997.

Risk scenario 2: an interrupted cycle on growth worries (most likely if the pockets of financial stress that have emerged broaden) is less friendly for risk assets initially, with possible relief later as in 2015.

Risk scenario 3: if growth keeps holding up, this could be the start of a more extended tightening driven by an investment boom as in 1999, and the longer it runs the greater the risk of a meaningful growth downgrade later.
The report lists 18 open GS cross-asset trade ideas, mostly FX and rates in EM and G10, plus one equity pair trade and one closed trade (ODF29).

risk_factors: Pockets of financial stress that have emerged could broaden into a wider issue and interrupt the hiking cycle on growth worries.
Resilient growth driven by an investment boom could extend the tightening cycle, raising the risk of a larger growth downgrade later, as after 1999.
Oil price relief is likely required for the inflation relief in GS baseline and in the most positive scenario.
Equity valuations (Shiller P/E 41) are similar to 1999, and core inflation (3.0%) is higher than at the start of the 1997, 1999 and 2015 cycles.
Small sample and differing macro shocks across past cycles limit the usefulness of historical analogues.
vol_and_positioning: GS notes pockets of financial stress have emerged. If they broaden into a wider issue, this is the path most likely to interrupt the hiking cycle on growth worries.

tension_points.bull_case: Modest hikes, growth around potential and gradual inflation relief imply a modestly positive path for equities. A shorter cycle on inflation relief would be the most positive, like 1997.
tension_points.bear_case: If growth holds up, the cycle could extend as in 1999, with a larger growth downgrade later. If financial stress broadens, an interrupted cycle would be less friendly for risk assets initially, as in 2015.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Broadening of the pockets of financial stress into a wider growth concern, or continued resilient growth that extends hiking beyond the modest baseline.

theme_stances.key_argument: A modest number of hikes, stable growth and gradual inflation relief imply a modestly positive path for equities.
theme_stances.evidence: modestly positive path for equities from here
